title: Effects of Payment on User Engagement in Online Courses
authors: Ali Goli; Pradeep K. Chintagunta; Srinivasaraghavan Sriram
eligible_reason: Not a staggered-adoption DiD. The 'treatment' is a user-specific event (crossing the course passing grade) interacted with a time-invariant paying-user indicator, plus a four-week post-payment window with an imposed linear decay. Fixed effects are user-course and quiz-by-paid-status; there are no calendar-time fixed effects. Every specification also includes a lagged-outcome control (prior cumulative time investment, with quiz-specific coefficients). No binary treatment switching on at unit-specific calendar dates with unit and calendar-time FE.
design_notes: Quiz-block-level panel of Coursera users (2012-2016, 70+ courses). Equation 1: log(1+I_iq) = alpha*Paying_i*BeforeCrossing_iq + xi*BeforeCrossing_iq + omega*WithinFourWeeksAfterPayment_iq + gamma*(t_iq - tau_i)*WithinFourWeeksAfterPayment_iq + eta_i (user-course FE) + eta_{q,delta_i} (quiz x paid FE) + beta_{-q}*log(1+I_{i,-q}) (prior investment) + e. Tables 2-3 (full sample, conditional on passing), Table 5 (alternative thresholds), Tables 6-9 (forum activity, peer effects, churn), Table 10 (grades). Column 3 of Tables 2-3 uses a boosted-tree propensity, 5:1 nearest-neighbor matched sample. Table 4 regresses estimated user FE on ability tiers (cross-sectional).
estimators_reported: OLS with user-course and quiz-by-paid FE plus lagged-outcome control

ineligible_specs.outcome: log(1 + time investment in quiz block)
ineligible_specs.treatment_var: Paying user x Before crossing passing grade (alpha); Weeks after payment (omega); decay (gamma)
ineligible_specs.fe: user-course FE, quiz x paid FE
ineligible_specs.controls: prior cumulative investment log(1+I_{i,-q}) with quiz-specific coefficients (lagged outcome)
ineligible_specs.exclusion_reason: no calendar-time FE; treatment is a user-specific threshold event, not an adoption date; lagged-outcome control

data_availability_statement: None found in the article text. Data are Coursera clickstream, quiz and payment records for courses offered by a large public university, plus Coursera survey data.
screener_notes: Full-text hits for 'difference-in-differences' come from the keyword list and from describing the paying/nonpaying comparison; 'staggered' appears only in the implications section ('staggered payments'). No replication package listed in the batch. Not a candidate for re-estimation.
